title: Analysis of Targeted Viral Protein Nanoparticles Delivered to HER2+ Tumors
protocol: Mix HerDox with sterile saline to prepare 0.2 ml of a 0.004 mg/kg dose per injection for an NU/NU mouse.
Draw the HerDox mixture into a 3/10 cc insulin syringe fitted with a 29G needle, avoiding bubbles.
Induce anesthesia by exposing the mouse to isoflurane in an induction chamber equipped with a gas scavenging system (Oxygen flow rates: 0.5-1 L/min, isoflurane concentration: 3-4%).
Inject the entire mixture into the tail vein of an anesthetized mouse.
Repeat injections on the same mouse for six more sequential days, once per day.
Turn on the Multimode In vivo Optical Imager.
Select an emission bandpass filter (590 nm ± 30 nm) suited for doxorubicin fluorescence detection.
Turn on Argon-Krypton laser and place an excitation bandpass filter (488 nm ± 10 nm) at the laser optical path.
Turn on the anesthesia system and then place a mouse into the anesthetizing chamber equipped with a gas scavenging system (Oxygen flow rates: 0.5-1 L/min, isoflurane concentration: 3-4%).
Transfer the mouse from the anesthetizing chamber to the imaging chamber.
Place a nosecone over the mouse's nose and open the flow for continuous anesthesia during image acquisition.
Acquire fluorescence images using an exposure time of 5-15 seconds.
Perform background correction or contrast adjustment in the image analysis.
Turn on the Multimode In vivo Optical Imager.
Select an emission bandpass filter (580 nm ± 20 nm) for Doxorubicin fluorescence detection.
Turn on Argon-Krypton laser and place an excitation bandpass filter (488 nm ±10 nm) at the laser optical path.
Place tumors and specific organs arranged on a Petri-dish into the imaging chamber.
Acquire fluorescence images of tissues using an exposure time of 5-15 seconds.
Repeat image acquisition with an empty Petri-dish to serve as background.
Perform image analysis and processing including background correction or contrast adjustment.
Turn on a Leica SPE confocal microscope.
Select 488 nm laser light for excitation of doxorubicin.
Select emission wavelengths (560-620 nm) for doxorubicin fluorescence detection.
Select a 40X or 63X objective and drop immersion oil on the objective lens.
Extract fresh tumors from euthanized mice that previously received HerDox and mock treatments.
Place tumors on a Petri-dish on ice to avoid tissue degradation.
Transfer tumors to a Delta T chamber for confocal imaging.
Acquire confocal images of the tumors at sequential focal depths (step size: 1 μm, thickness: 20 μm).
Perform maximum intensity z-projection of the images.
Calculate mean fluorescence intensities of the maximum intensity Z-projection images using ImageJ.
Power on a laser scanning fluorescence confocal microscope.
Acquire 15 images of HerDox-treated tumors at a specified depth within the spectral range of 510-650 nm, with a step size of 10 nm, and excitation at 488 nm light.
Acquire 15 images of untreated tumors at a specified depth within the spectral range of 510-650 nm, with a step size of 10 nm, and excitation at 488 nm light.
Prepare a 100 μM solution of doxorubicin.
Perform spectral imaging of the 100 μM doxorubicin solution to obtain the pure spectral signature of Dox fluorescence (spectral range: 510-650 nm, step size: 10 nm).
Acquire an autofluorescence spectral signature from an image cube obtained by spectral imaging of untreated tumors (spectral range: 510-650 nm, step size: 10 nm).
Generate four reference spectral signatures using a program.
Plot pure autofluorescence as one reference spectral signature.
Mix 10 μM doxorubicin with 90 μM autofluorescence to generate the second reference spectral signature (0.1.doxyrubicin + 0.9.autofluorescence).
Mix 20 μM doxorubicin with 80 μM autofluorescence to generate the third reference spectral signature (0.2.doxyrubicin + 0.8.autofluorescence).
Mix 30 μM doxorubicin with 70 μM autofluorescence to generate the fourth reference spectral signature (0.3.doxyrubicin + 0.7.autofluorescence).
Perform spectral classification of the images using a previously developed program through Euclidean distance measure based on reference spectral signatures.
Perform linear spectral unmixing of the images using a spectral unmixing program (plug-in in ImageJ) we developed for comparison with ratiometric spectral imaging and analysis.
